old_digest: If a Striker is hurt, some other person may be allowed to stand out for him, but not go in. Or, if the Ball is struck up, and he wilfully strikes it again. If the Ball is struck up, the Striker may guard his Wicket either with his Bat or his body. *** In Single-wicket matches, if the Striker moves out of his ground to strike the Ball, he shall be allowed no notch for such stroke.
new_digest: If a striker is hurt some person may be allowed to stand out for him, but not go in. If the ball is struck up, the striker may guard his wicket either with his bat or his body. In single wicket matches, if the striker moves out of his ground to strike the ball, he shall be allowed no notch for such stroke.

old_digest: The Umpires, in all matches, to pitch fair Wickets, and the parties to toss for the choice of Innings.
The Umpire at the Bowler’s Wicket shall be first applied to, to decide on all catches.
new_digest: That the umpire at the bowler’s wicket be first applied to, to decide on all catches.

old_digest: Must be opposite to each other, at the distance of twenty-two yards, which shall be pitched within thirty yards of a centre fixed by the adversaries.
new_digest: Must be opposite to each other, at the distance of twenty-two yards.

old_digest: must be bowled underhand, and delivered with the hand below the elbow. A 3 In the event of a change of bowling, no more than two Balls are to be allowed in practice. The Bowler who takes the two Balls, to be obliged to bowl four Balls.

law_title: THE PARTY WHICH GOES FROM HOME
new_digest: Shall have the choice of the innings, and the pitching of the wickets, which shall be pitched within thirty yards of a centre fixed by the adversaries. When the parties meet at a third place, the bowlers shall toss up for the pitching of the wickets and the choice of going in. It shall not be lawful for either party, during a match, without the consent of the other, to alter the ground by rolling, watering, covering, mowing, or beating. This rule is not meant to prevent the striker from beating the ground with his bat, near where he stands, during the innings, or to prevent the bowler from filling up the holes, watering his ground, or using sawdust, &c. when the ground is wet.

old_digest: Shall deliver the Ball with one foot behind the Bowling-crease, and within the Return-crease, and shall bowl four Balls before he changes wickets, which he shall do but once in the same Innings. If the Bowler tosses the Ball over the Striker’s head, or bowls it so wide that the Striker cannot play at it, the party that is in shall be allowed one notch, to be put down to the Byes, and those Balls not to be reckoned as any of the four Balls. If the Bowler bowls a No Ball, the Striker may play at it, and be allowed all the runs he can get, and shall not be put out, except by running out.
new_digest: Shall deliver the ball with one foot behind the bowling-crease, and within the return crease, and shall bowl four or six balls before he changes wickets, which he shall do but once in the same innings.
